BR13A grillage — parametric model

M7–M12 southbound exit ramp, 30 m single span on a 34.5° skew, four 1515 deep PSC Super-T girders. Every tab of the Excel takeoff is here, plus the grillage mesh, section designer, load combinations, hog and member properties. Values read from the drawings are locked — open the padlock to override one, and it is marked as an override.

AS 5100.2 Combination Builder

 
Tick the load cases in your bridge model. Every ULS and SLS combination is generated as its own row, one signed factor per load case, then exported to Excel, MIDAS Civil, SPACE GASS or Strand7. Directions (+X / −X, +Y / −Y, up / down) are applied by the combinations, so each directional load is defined once in your model.






 
Step 1Load cases in your project

 
Define each load case once, acting in the positive direction shown. Factors are AS 5100.2 Table D1 / D3 values and can be edited. "Beneficial" applies to permanent loads only.

RulesHow the load cases are combined

 
    
 
    Confirm against your licensed copy: whether Cl. 15 states its own orthogonal earthquake rule; how wind directions combine (Cl. 17: separately, or vertical with horizontal); the multiple-track factors (the original 2017 Table 9.4 gives 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.85 / 0.70 / 0.60, Amendment 2 revised Cl. 9.3). Not generated: fatigue, construction, fire, ship impact, mining subsidence.

    Strand layout – Super-T defaults from TfNSW B0203 Sheet B (T1 750, T2 1000, T3 1200, T4 1500, T5 1825)

    Longitudinal reinforcement (used by the detailed method)
    

    One row per line: level above soffit : bar Ø : x offsets (same x syntax as strands). E.g. 60: 20: ±325. Bars are bonded over the full length; area πd²/4. Defaults: Super-T bottom 3 × Ø20 per side, top flange Ø12 at ≤160 spacing, Ø12 in each web; TfNSW planks Q3 bars from B0303–B0314.
    


      
    

    Beam & section properties
    

    Concrete (cl. 3.1)
    Strand & time-dependent
    

    

    Deck stage & superimposed loads
    Stage C: wet deck + formwork on the girder alone from the pour. Stage D: from pour + hardening time, girder and deck act compositely for all later effects (creep restraint, differential shrinkage, later prestress losses, SIDL). Values shown are demo defaults – replace every value with project data.
    

    Longitudinal section – strand debonding
    

    Section check – SLS crack control, steel stresses & shear (cl. 8.6.2.1)
    

    Permanent state (prestress after losses, self-weight, deck, SIDL, creep, shrinkage) comes from the detailed time-step analysis at the chosen location and age. Load cases are additional actions on top of it: N* (kN, + compression, at the transformed centroid), V* (kN), M* (kNm, sagging +). Class 1 = cl. 8.6.2.1 main (≤ 0.25√f'c); Class 2 = 8.6.2.1(a) (≤ 0.5√f'c with bonded steel ≤ 200 c/c near the tensile face); Class 3 = 8.6.2.1(b) (cracked section, steel stress increment from decompression ≤ Table 8.6.2.1).
